subjects.name: Real Property Characteristics, Legal Descriptions, and Property Use

chapters.name: Real vs. Personal Property and Legal Descriptions
chapters.summary: Fixtures, trade fixtures, and emblements; the physical and economic characteristics of land; and the three methods of legal description, including the rectangular survey.
keyPoints: A fixture is attached personal property that becomes part of the real estate.
A township has 36 sections, and a section has 640 acres.

chapters.name: Public and Private Land Use Controls
chapters.summary: Police power, eminent domain, taxation, and escheat; zoning, variances, and nonconforming uses; CC&Rs, easements, licenses, and encroachments.
keyPoints: Zoning is an exercise of police power.
An easement in gross benefits a person or company, such as a utility.

subjects.name: Forms of Ownership, Transfer, and Recording of Title

chapters.name: Ownership, Estates, and Liens
chapters.summary: Freehold and leasehold estates, life estates, co-ownership such as joint tenancy and tenancy in common, condominiums and cooperatives, and lien types and priority.
keyPoints: Joint tenancy needs the four unities and includes the right of survivorship.
Property tax liens usually have first priority.

chapters.name: Deeds, Title Transfer, and Recording
chapters.summary: Elements and types of deeds, voluntary and involuntary alienation, recording and notice, chain of title, title insurance, and clearing a cloud on title.
keyPoints: Title passes when the deed is delivered and accepted.
Recording gives constructive notice.

chapters.name: Value, Appraisal, and Estimating Value
chapters.summary: Market value and price, principles of value, the appraisal process, the sales comparison, cost, and income approaches, depreciation, GRM, and CMAs and BPOs.
keyPoints: Adjust the comparable, not the subject: comparable better, subtract.
Value = net operating income ÷ cap rate.

chapters.name: Contracts
chapters.summary: Types and elements of contracts, performance and breach, the Statute of Frauds, offers and counteroffers, earnest money, contingencies, options, and remedies.
keyPoints: A contract to sell real estate must be in writing to be enforceable.
Any change to an offer is a counteroffer that rejects the original offer.

chapters.name: Agency Relationships and Duties
chapters.summary: Principals and customers, creating and ending agency, fiduciary duties, duties to customers, dual agency, and disclosure of conflicts of interest.
keyPoints: Fiduciary duties: obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, reasonable care.
Known material defects must be disclosed to customers as well.

chapters.name: Brokerage Agreements and Risk Management
chapters.summary: Listing and buyer agreements, trust funds, scope of practice, antitrust, Do Not Call rules, independent contractor status, vicarious liability, and E&O insurance.
keyPoints: Under an exclusive right-to-sell listing, the broker is paid whoever sells.
Competing brokers may never agree on commission rates.

chapters.name: Fair Housing
chapters.summary: Protected classes under federal law, steering, blockbusting, redlining, advertising, disability modifications and accommodations, and enforcement.
keyPoints: The Fair Housing Act protects race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, and familial status.
The Civil Rights Act of 1866 bars all racial discrimination with no exceptions.

chapters.name: Property Disclosures and Environmental Issues
chapters.summary: Material facts and defects, lead-based paint rules for pre-1978 housing, radon, asbestos, underground storage tanks, flood zones, CERCLA, and site assessments.
keyPoints: Housing built before 1978 needs a lead-based paint disclosure.
CERCLA (Superfund) can make current owners liable for cleanup.

chapters.name: Financing and Settlement
chapters.summary: Notes and mortgages, loan clauses, the secondary market, conventional and government loans, PMI, TRID, RESPA, Regulation Z, ECOA, and seller financing.
keyPoints: PMI is usually needed on a conventional loan above 80% LTV.
The Closing Disclosure must arrive at least 3 business days before closing.

chapters.name: Real Estate Math
chapters.summary: Area and acreage, commission splits, LTV, points, property tax, net to seller, prorations, PITI, cap rate, and return on investment.
keyPoints: 1 acre = 43,560 square feet.
One discount point = 1% of the loan amount.
